findings.impact: Any code execution or credential exfiltration in the API container - and the sibling services in this tree show several such paths - is immediately full administrative control of the production AWS account: reading every bucket and secret, creating IAM principals, and deleting the data stack.
findings.recommendation: Replace the tier mapping with a least-privilege policy naming the specific actions and resource ARNs the API uses. If migrations and break-glass tooling genuinely need broader rights, give them a separate role assumed by a separate task, guarded by a permissions boundary.

triage.reason: No permissions boundary, SCP or condition appears in the tree; addManagedPolicy at service-role.ts:45 is unqualified.
The comment at environments.ts:66-67 declares the intent, but nothing bounds it: the same role serves ordinary API traffic, not only the runbook commands.
fromAwsManagedPolicyName('AdministratorAccess') resolves to the real AWS managed policy granting Action:* Resource:*.

findings.unaided_label: beacon-cdk: prod API task role gets AdministratorAccess

findings.title: Production bucket policy grants anonymous read of every object in the shared bucket
findings.evidence: When publicRead is true the construct both weakens the public-access block - blockPublicPolicy and restrictPublicBuckets set to false (lines 37-38) - and adds a resource policy granting s3:GetObject to new iam.AnyPrincipal() over this.bucket.arnForObjects('*') (lines 56-63): every object, not a prefix. DataStack passes publicRead: cfg.assetsPublic (data-stack.ts:29) and prod sets assetsPublic: true (config/environments.ts:64). The same file's comment at data-stack.ts:26-27 says this one bucket holds 'the brand assets the CDN pulls, the rendered documents and the tenant data exports'.
findings.impact: Every rendered customer document and every tenant data export in production is anonymously readable by anyone who knows or guesses the key. The intent recorded in the comment was to publish brand assets; the statement published the whole bucket.
findings.recommendation: Scope the statement to the assets prefix (arnForObjects('assets/*')) at minimum, and better, put the CDN in front with an Origin Access Control and keep BLOCK_ALL on the bucket. Separate tenant documents and exports into their own private bucket.

triage.reason: The exposure is intended for brand assets only; the resource ARN makes it unbounded, so the 'intended and bounded' condition fails on the second half.
The same bucket holds rendered documents and tenant exports per data-stack.ts:26-27.
The construct explicitly disables the two block-public-access flags that would otherwise neutralise the policy (bucket.ts:37-38).

findings.unaided_label: beacon-cdk: assetsPublic makes the whole shared bucket world-readable

findings.title: The API task role is granted read, write and delete over the entire bucket
findings.evidence: grantArtifacts(serviceRole.role, props.artifacts.bucket) is called with the prefix argument omitted, so it defaults to '' (lib/constructs/service-role.ts:55) and the policy resources become bucket.arnForObjects('*') with s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject and s3:DeleteObject (service-role.ts:57-62), plus ListBucket with an 's3:prefix': ['*'] condition. The function's own docstring at service-role.ts:49-51 instructs the caller to pass the prefix 'so the grant stays scoped to it'.
findings.impact: The API service can read, overwrite and delete every object in the bucket shared by all services and all tenants, including rendered documents and data exports belonging to tenants it is not serving.
findings.recommendation: Pass the prefix the API actually writes under (grantArtifacts(role, bucket, `${cfg.name}/api/`)), and split the bucket per data class so a prefix mistake cannot reach tenant exports.

triage.reason: No bucket policy in the tree narrows the principal's access; the only resource policy added widens it (bucket.ts:56).
The construct provides the scoping mechanism and documents it; the omission is not a declared exception.
This is the load-bearing control on cross-tenant object access from the API, not defence in depth.

findings.title: API container is configured for wildcard CORS with credentials
findings.evidence: The container environment sets CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN: '*' together with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: 'true' (lines 59-60), with the comment that 'the origin cannot be pinned'. Browsers reject literal '*' when credentials are allowed, so an application honouring both settings must either break or - the usual resolution, and the one the comment's requirement implies - reflect the request Origin instead, which is the same defect the sibling nginx configuration in edge-relay has.
findings.impact: Whichever way the application resolves the contradiction, the declared policy is that any origin may make credentialed requests. If it reflects the Origin, any web page reads authenticated API responses in a victim's session.
findings.recommendation: Enumerate the tenant subdomain pattern and validate the Origin against an anchored expression server-side, emitting the matched origin only; never pair a wildcard with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials.

triage.reason: The API image (beacon/api:1.12.0) is not in this tree, so how it interprets the two variables cannot be read. The declared configuration is the finding.
The API is credential-bearing by the second variable's own admission.
'Origins cannot be pinned' is a requirement, not a bound on the exposure.

findings.title: RDS instance is declared publicly accessible
findings.evidence: publiclyAccessible: true on the Postgres DatabaseInstance (line 60), with the comment that an analytics warehouse in another account 'pulls nightly over the public endpoint'. This assigns the instance a public IP and a publicly-resolving endpoint. Two controls in the same tree push back: vpcSubnets is PRIVATE_ISOLATED (line 48), a subnet type CDK creates with no route to an internet gateway, and the security group allows 5432 only from serviceSg and bastionSg (lib/network-stack.ts:76-85).
findings.impact: As declared, the instance is not reachable from the internet because the isolated subnet has no IGW route and the security group admits only two internal groups. The defect is that the instance is configured to be public and is prevented from being so by two settings elsewhere: adding a route, moving the subnet, or widening the security group turns it into a directly-exposed production database, with none of those changes looking like a security change.
findings.recommendation: Set publiclyAccessible: false and give the cross-account warehouse a PrivateLink endpoint or a VPC peering path with a scoped security-group rule.

triage.reason: Two independent controls prevent reachability today: the PRIVATE_ISOLATED subnet placement (data-stack.ts:48) and the security group's two ingress rules (network-stack.ts:76-85). This is why the finding is medium and probable rather than high and confirmed - per FP-10 it is downgraded, not deleted.
The declaration is a latent exposure that becomes real on any routing or subnet change.
The stated intent - a nightly cross-account pull - does not require a public endpoint; PrivateLink covers it.

findings.title: Bastion accepts SSH from anywhere in dev, and dev is the fallback environment
findings.evidence: dev.adminCidrs is ['0.0.0.0/0'] (line 36), and NetworkStack turns each entry into an ingress rule on tcp/22 for the bastion security group (lib/network-stack.ts:52-58). The bastion in turn is allowed to reach Postgres on 5432 (network-stack.ts:81-85). pickEnv compounds it: `environments[name ?? ''] ?? dev` (environments.ts:83) returns the dev configuration for a missing BEACON_ENV and for any misspelled value, and bin/beacon.ts:14 passes process.env.BEACON_ENV ?? app.node.tryGetContext('env') into it - so a typo in a pipeline variable silently synthesises the dev configuration.
findings.impact: The dev jump host accepts SSH from the whole internet, and through it the dev database. The silent fallback means the 0.0.0.0/0 rule is also what a deployment with an unset or mistyped BEACON_ENV produces.
findings.recommendation: Restrict dev.adminCidrs to the same office ranges the other environments use (or use SSM Session Manager and drop port 22 entirely), and make pickEnv throw on an unknown name instead of defaulting.

triage.reason: The dev configuration is in the shipped stack set and is what pickEnv returns by default; it is not excluded from any build.
Port 22 to a jump host is not a public-load-balancer exposure; the bastion is an administrative surface.
The bastion has a path to the dev database (network-stack.ts:81).
